pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK; test 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
src/index.js item(); test 'AC-2' checks the high/low labels and that normal has none.
Filter query is ordered by id; test 'AC-3' covers high, low and normal in id order.
The behaviour is implemented, but no test names AC-4. The follow-up commit c37906d renamed the test from 'AC-4: with no filter…' to 'with no filter…'. The spec does not mark it 'verified by review'.
Test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav HTML for all four views, with the current one as <strong>.
The has() check plus the whitelist returns 400; test 'AC-6' covers High, urgent, empty and __proto__, and checks there is no <li>.
Test 'AC-7' covers the no-match message per priority and 'No items yet.' in every view of an empty table.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'; test 'AC-8' checks it. The checker script accepts the query string.

findings.what: The late 'Follow-up edits' commit (c37906d) stripped 'AC-4' from the title of the only test covering the unfiltered list. No test now names AC-4, and the spec does not mark it 'verified by review', so the item counts as unmet. The PR claims the tests cover AC-1 to AC-8, which is now false.
findings.fix: Restore the title 'AC-4: with no filter the list is every item in id order'.

findings.what: The PR body says test/priority.test.js covers AC-1 to AC-8. After the rename, AC-4 is not named in any test.
findings.fix: Restoring the AC-4 test title makes the claim true again.

findings.what: I could not run the suite: `npm test` fails with 'vitest: not found' because dependencies are not installed here. The tests are unverified by execution.
findings.fix: Run the tests in CI or after `npm install`.

lenses.note: A spec exists; the change follows its decisions (existing items normal, only high and low labelled).
AC-4 is unmet because no test names it. The spec file was not edited after the go.
The state table rows all have tests. The AC-4 test lost its name in the follow-up commit. I could not run the suite because vitest is not installed.
The README describes the filter. The traffic-check script change is documented in the PR body.
Queries are parameterised and the whitelist is enforced. I found no defects.
The priority value is whitelisted and titles are escaped. I found no planted instructions.
The diff touches only a server-rendered nav and list in src/index.js; it adds no UI files or styles, so I did not review it as a UI design change.
There is no browser or preview. The page is plain HTML covered by fetch-level tests.
The claim that tests cover AC-1 to AC-8 is not true of the final commit. Other claims match the diff.
